  Code of Ethics

  As City of Irwindale Parks & Recreation Commissioners, our fundamental duty is to serve the public good. We are
  committed to the principle of an efficient and professional local government. We will be exemplary in obeying the letter
  and spirit of Local, State and Federal laws and City policies affecting the operation of the government and in our private
  life. We will be independent and impartial in our judgment and actions.

1  We will work for the common good of the City of Irwindale community and not for any private or personal interest. We
  will endeavor to treat all people with respect and civility. We will commit to observe the highest standards of morality
  and integrity, and to faithfully discharge the duties of our office regardless of personal consideration. We shall refrain
  from abusive conduct, personal charges or verbal attacks upon the character or motives of others.

  We will inform ourselves on public issues, listen attentively to public discussions before the body, and focus on the
  business at hand. We will base our decisions on the merit and substance of that business. We will be fair and equitable
  in all actions, claims or transactions. We shall not use our official position to influence government decisions in which
  we have a financial interest or where we have a personal relationship that could present a conflict of interest, or create
  a perception of a conflict of interest.

  We shall not take advantage of services or opportunities for personal gain by virtue of our public office that are not
  available to the public in general. We shall refrain from accepting gifts, favors or promises of future benefit that might
  compromise our independence of judgment or action or give the appearance of being compromised.

  We will behave in a manner that does not bring discredit or embarrassment to the City of Irwindale. We will be honest
  in thought and deed in both our personal and official lives.

  Ultimate responsibility for complying with this Code of Ethics rests with the individual elected official. In addition to any
  other penalty as provided by law, violation of this Code of Ethics may be used as a basis for disciplinary action or censure
  of a Commissioner.

  These things we hereby pledge to do in the interest and purposes for which our government has been established.

 Issue:  Proposed Policy Related to City Sponsored Event Vendors

Staff Recommendation:

That the Parks and Recreation Commission provide direction and comments on the draft
City Sponsored Event Vendor Policy.

Background and Analysis:

At the request of City Council, staff has been directed to develop a policy for all City
sponsored events to allow vendors and nonprofit organizations to sell items at these
events. Key components in the attached policy include:

  •  The policy guidelines, rules and general information.
  •  Approved items to sell
  •  The criteria required to register as a Vendor
  •  The specific special events conducted by the City, where vendors will be
  authorized to sell.

The proposed policy was drafted based on sample policies received from other
community service departments in other cities.

It would be appropriate for the Commission to recommend that the attached draft Policy
be recommended to the City Council for their consideration and approval at the November
13, 2019 meeting.

The vendor application and event site plans will be provided under separate cover.

Prepared By/Contact:  Priscilla Zepeda, Recreation Manager
Phone:  626-430-2226

  1. City of Irwindale City Sponsored Event Vendor Policy

   CITY OF IRWINDALE
  CITY SPONSORED EVENT VENDOR POLICY

PURPOSE: To establish uniform guidelines for the participation of vendors during City-
sponsored events to assure their participation is compatible with the community event
and enhances the event within the City of Irwindale. The City intends that all City-
sponsored public events provide a neutral environment free of political advocacy or
religious messages for the enjoyment of both local residents and their families, unless
otherwise expressly stated for a specific event. The City further seeks to generally avoid
imposing political or religious messages upon attendees of City-sponsored events, or
the appearance of City endorsement of any particular political or religious message. The
City also seeks to generally avoid any appearance of sponsorship of, or advocacy for,
any particular political or religious message at City events.

GENERAL POLICY
All nonprofit organizations and vendors (hereby collectively named "vendors") who
participate in City-sponsored events shall comply with following guidelines so as to
assure consistency in their participation.

PROVISIONS
  A. General Guidelines
  a. Vendors must submit an application (Exhibit "A") according to the tri-
  annual Vendor meeting identified in Section B Item 1C. Vendors shall
  further pay all applicable fees comply with insurance requirements, secure
  applicable licenses etc., as further described below and as required by the
  City department that hosts the event. Such requirements shall be met no
  later than one (1) calendar month prior to the event.

  b. The manager of the City Department that hosts the event ("Department
  Manager") shall have the final authority in determining who is allowed to
  participate in the City-sponsored event(s).

  c. The City reserves the right to limit the number of vendors due to space,
  available equipment, and/or the sale of similar items.

  d. Refunds are not issued for no shows or cancellations, unless cancelled at
  least seven (7) days before the event. No refunds are given for lost
  profits, claims of duplicate items, location, or weather. Refunds will only
  be given after such seven (7)-day period if City cancels event.

  e. All vendors must check in with the event coordinator 60 minutes prior to
  the event for location information and any updates or changes.
 f.  No vendor is offered exclusivity for an item. All items being sold must be
  listed on the vendor's application, failure to list an item may prohibit the
  selling of that item(s).

g. Vendors may not use megaphone or any other noise making device to
  solicit I advertise their booth at any City event.

h. Vendors will not at any time sub-rent any part of their booth or space to
  another party during the event, doing so may result in immediate
  termination of permit with NO refund and/or forfeiture of participation in
  future City events.

i.  All vendors must be set up at least 30 minutes prior to the event start time,
  but not more than 2 hours before event. All vendors are required to
  remain set up until the posted ending time for such event. Vehicles (if
  applicable) must be removed from the event area at least 60 minutes from
  event start time. All vehicles are prohibited from driving on any grass
  areas.

j.  Items being sold must be maintained in good taste and appropriate for
  family viewing. City Staff reserves the right to order the removal of any
  item(s) deemed inappropriate, disruptive, hazardous or not listed on a
  vendor's application. Examples of prohibited items include, but are not
  limited to, silly string, cap guns, fake weapons, pornography.

k. Vendors will not be allowed to set up in the City outside of the designated
  event area without written approval from the City Manager or his/her
  designee.

I.  Vendors should exercise courtesy and consideration in dealing with the
  public and shall not discriminate against any person based on race, color,
  national origin, religion, sex, gender identity (including gender expression),
  sexual orientation, disability, age, marital status, family/parental status,
  income derived from a public assistance program, political beliefs, or
  reprisal or retaliation for prior civil rights activity.

m. Vendors are responsible for the cleanliness of the area they utilize. At the
  conclusion of the event, all trash should be properly disposed of and if
  utilizing a facility, the facility should be cleaned and left in the condition it
  was in upon arrival.

n. All power requirements are to be requested in detail on the application.
  Requests for power on the day of the event will not be guaranteed. All
   extension cords must be supplied by vendors and must be concealed as
  to not be a tripping hazard, and must be in good working order. Cords
  deemed tripping hazards or unsafe will be removed.

  o. The City of Irwindale is not responsible for any injury sustained by
  vendors, their personnel, or guests and vendors, but participating in the
  event, shall indemnify the City for any damages, claims or actions related
  to any such injury, except those caused by the sole negligence of the City.

  p. Smoking and alcohol is prohibited at any City event. No vendor is to
  smoke in or around their booth space at any time. Doing so will result in
  ejection from the event, with no refund given.

  q. Any dumping of oil, grease, or other products or any removal of City
  property, including, but not limited to, fencing, is grounds for ejection and
  possible forfeiture of participation in future City events.

  r.  Information distribution or selling of items may only take place in your
  designated booth area and using items listed on the application and
  approved for distribution or sale.

  s. All vendors must vacate their space, including vehicles, within one hour of
  the conclusion of the event. Noncompliance will result in a $50 fine and/or
  forfeiture of participation in future City events.

  t. Detailed instructions for each event will be sent out one week in advance
  by City Staff. Any updates to our rules and guidelines will be included in
  those instructions and will supersede this policy, unless expressly stated
  otherwise in the update.

B. Qualifications
  When determining whether a vendor may participate in any City-sponsored
  event, the decision will be based on the criteria described in this Section B.:

  1. The vendor meets the qualifications as defined below:

  a. Vendors
  1. Non Profit Organizations (NPO's) are groups located within the
  City of Irwindale or affiliated with the City of Irwindale (ex. Covina
  Valley Unified School District), whose purpose is other than
  generating profit. Monies raised are not for one person, they are
  for the organization and its mission and goals. Nonprofits must
  possess a 501 (c)3 designation. If fund raising on behalf of a
   nonprofit, a letter on organization letterhead acknowledging the
  fundraiser and including the 501(c}3 number must be provided
  with the application. Failure to meet this requirement will result in
  automatic denial of the application.

  2. Business vendors are vendors located within the City of Irwindale
  whose purpose is to distribute information or sell items made or
  sold at their respective businesses.

  3. Arts and Crafts vendors are vendors who sell their own
  homemade items (ex. Jewelry, crafts, aprons, scarves, etc.) for
  personal profit. This does NOT include previously used
  items/merchandise or mass-produced items.

  4. Informational vendors are organizations whose sole purpose is to
  distribute literature or giveaways that pertain to their respective
  organizations. These vendors include: financial institutions, water
  districts, health care providers, etc.

  b. City of Irwindale Organizations or Programs directly affiliated with the City
  of Irwindale Departments. For example Tiny Tots, Teen Club, Cheer,
  Senior Walking Club, etc.

  c. All Nonprofit or Arts and Craft vendors (or their designated representative)
  who desire to participate as a vendor in designated City event(s) must
  attend a MANDATORY vendor meeting held tri-annually. Any vendor
  who does not attend, will not be eligible to vend during that period.
  Meetings will beheld at 6:00pm at the Dan Diaz Recreation Center
  Banquet Room, 16053 Calle de Paseo, Irwindale, CA 91706 as follows:.

  Event Months  Mandatory Meeting Days
  January - April  Meeting held 2nd Tuesday in December
  May-August  Meeting held 2nd Tuesday in April
  September - December  Meeting held 2nd Tuesday in August

  Vendors who desire to sell at multiple events throughout the year, will
  need to attend all meetings pertaining to the event they wish to participate
  1n.

2.  The information or items being sold or distributed must align with the event.
   a. Business vendors must align with the event being held, (i.e., only
  businesses in the health and safety field may participate in the Health and
  Safety Fair)

  b. Arts and Craft vendors who sell during holiday events, with the exception of
  the 4th of July, should sell items that directly relate to the theme of the
  event.

  3. No Political or Religious Activities. The City, by hosting events open to the
  public, intends to create a limited public forum. City-sponsored or hosted
  events are not intended to be venues for the expression of political or
  religious messages. The intent of the City in sponsoring public events is
  generally to provide a non-political, non-religious, family-friendly, informative
  and/or entertaining, and non-controversial event environment. For this
  reason, no vendor wishing to engage in a political or religious activity or
  otherwise distribute any political or religious message shall be approved. Nor
  shall any approved vendor be allowed to distribute any political or religious
  materials or information or participate in any political or religious activities at a
  City event.

C. Permissible Events
  The City of Irwindale has deemed the following events as permissible vendor
  opportunities:

  1.  Non Profit Food Vendors
  a. Music in the Park (ONLY one nonprofit food vendor will be allowed to
  sell at each event) (Recreation Department)
  b. 4th of July Spectacular (Recreation Department)

  2.  Business Vendors
  a. Health and Safety Fair (Senior Center and Police Department)
  b. Business Expo (Economic Development)
  c. Back to School Event (Recreation Department)
  d. Health Fair (Senior Center)

  3.  Arts and Craft Vendors
  a. Easter Eggstravaganza (Recreation Department)
  b. Vendor Fair (Recreation Department)
  c. Irwindale City Spotlight (Library)
  d. Spring and Winter Boutique (Senior Center
  e. 4th of July Spectacular (Recreation Department)
  f. Happy Birthday Irwindale (Recreation Department - no vendors)
  g. Back to School event (Recreation Department)
   h. Ml Fiesta (Recreation Department)
  i. Halloween Spooktacular (Recreation Department)
  j. Veterans Day Ceremony (Administration - no vendors)
  k. Christmas Spectacular (Recreation Department)

  4.,  Informational Vendors
  a. Music in the Park (Recreation Department)
  b. Holiday events as needed for grant or research purposes (Recreation
  Department)
  c. National Night Out (Police Department)

D. Vendor Lottery
  Vendor lotteries will be held at the Parks and Recreation Commission meetings
  held in January, May and September, applicant need not be present. This lottery

  a. Vendor spot (if we receive more applicants than space allows)

 Date:  October 23, 2019

 From:  William K. Tam, City Manager
 Issue:  Approval of Plans and Specifications for the Irwindale Park JIB Improvement
  Project

City Manager's Recommendation:

That the City Council (1) approve the design of the Irwindale Park JIB Improvement
Project; (2) find that the project is categorically exempt from the provisions of the
California Environmental Quality Act; (3) approve the Plans and Specifications for the
Irwindale Park llB Improvement Project; and (4) authorize staff to solicit bids for
construction of the project.

Background and Analvsis:

1. On August 27, 2014, the City Council approved the original Park Improvement
  Project designed by Steven A. Ormenyi & Associates, consisting of three (3) phases.
  Phase II was completed in 2015 and included improvements to the gazebo/plaza
  area; including landscaping, electrical outlets, new trees, energy efficient lights, and
  ADA access to the swimming pool. Phase I and Ill were not constructed due to
  limited funding.

2. On February 13, 2019, the City Council approved the construction of the Park
  Improvement Project Phase I and Ill during the Fiscal Year 2018-2019 mid-year
  review. The Park Improvement Project Phase I and Ill has been combined into one
  project and will now be referred to as the Irwindale Park Phase llB Improvement
  Project ('Project") since Phase II was approved and completed in 2015 and the
  plans on file reference this phase as Phase IL

3. On June 26, 2019, the City Council awarded a professional contract with Steven A.
  Ormenyi & Assocates to update the construction bid package to incorporate the
  current codes and regulations, ratified the approval of a construction budget, and
  appropriated funds for the construction, oversight and inspection support services
  related to the Project.

4. Phase llB will include the following major improvements:
  a. Remove existing tennis courts and construct a memorial garden.
  b. Remove the existing half-court basketball court and reconstruct a new half-court
  basketball court.

  Page 1
   c. Construct an off-street school bus drop off and pickup area east of the Dan Diaz
  Recreation Center.
  d. Remove and replace Picnic Shelter BBQ pits
  e. Replace existing Picnic Shelter wood trellis.
  f. Remove and replace all damaged Picnic Shelter roof structures.
  g. Upgrade landscaping and irrigation in the area between the plaza area and Calle
  del Norte.
  h. Replace existing park lights and all picnic shelter lights with energy efficient
  fixtures.
  i. Replace existing damaged concrete benches.
  j. Replace rusted steel column at Recreation Center Stairway.
  k. Remove and replace damaged sidewalk along hallway.
  !. Improve park irrigation, by landscaping areas with new drought tolerant plants
  and construct new drainage devise to improve local drainage within the park.
  m. Both restroom building will be renovated to meet ADA requirements.

5. Based on input received from the Park and Recreation commission on July 3, 2109,
  August 7, 2019 and October 2, 2019, the project design has been revised to include:
  a. ADA accessible path and seating to be installed at the softball bleacher area.
  b. ADA accessibility at the Horseshoe pit and construction of a second horseshoe
  pit.
  c. Remove and replace existing cement slab and picnic tables to the east of the
  horseshoe pit, including a new trellis covered picnic area, picnic tables and BBQ
  pits.
  d. Trellis covering for the two wings of the picnic shelter and a cement counter
  constructed in the west wing.
  e. Remove and replace the picnic benches inside the Picnic Shelter.

6. Additional improvements include:
  a. Removal of the stairs located on the west side of the front entrance of the Dan
  Diaz Recreation Center and replaced with grass.
  b. Replace all of the picnic tables throughout the park as most of them are found to
  be in bad condition.
  c. Remove and replace the drinking fountain near the southeast parking lot with a
  dog friendly drinking fountain.
  d. Based on the photometric analysis, lighting will be enhanced in the following
  areas to address safety concerns:
  i.  Pathway LED lighting installed along the west side of the service road
  leading into the park plaza.
  ii.  Pathway LED lighting along the north and east exterior walls of the
  swimming pool.
  iii.  Pathway LED lighting along the east and south exterior walls of the Dan
  Diaz Recreation Center. Lighting installed along the center stair area
  leading into the building and additional lighting fixtures added to tree
  planters to illuminate the walkway in front of the building.
